mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above trend for two consecutive quarters signals robust demand growth, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth exceeds trend for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically greater than zero during periods when GDPC1 exceeds trend for two quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE drops below 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both UNRATE and PAYEMS above their prior 12-month averages in the same month indicates strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both rise above 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both UNRATE and PAYEMS exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 6-month moving averages in the same month signals weakening consumer and investment demand, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both fall below 6-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both RSAFS and HOUST are below their 6-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month spike in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% with no prior warning in the previous three months signals an unexpected policy tightening, which shocks equity valuations and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps above 5% in one month with no prior increase in previous three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative following an unexpected FEDFUNDS jump above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent divergence between INDPRO and GDPC1, where INDPRO grows below trend while GDPC1 grows above trend for three consecutive months, signals a shift from manufacturing to services-led growth, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher-profit service sector weighting.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < trend and GDPC1 > trend for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO underperforms while GDPC1 outperforms for three consecutive months.
